top_choice_rationale: P004 (Cirac, Zoller, Blatt) rests on a complete architecture for ion-based quantum computation and simulation, proposed in 1995 and realised through three decades of independent confirmation, with a clear theory-plus-experiment allocation. The 2012 prize honoured the enabling control methods, whereas this recognises gate-based computation and simulation built on them; the overlap argument is real but not decisive. P001 follows for its predicted-then-observed flat-band chain despite youth and unsettled mechanism, then P003 for maturity but contested credit and the 2016 overlap, then P002 as sound but close to the 2005 and 2012 precision-measurement prizes. A prize is preferable to none, so P000 is last.
recusal_note: Possible perception of interest on P004: professional work in superconducting quantum computing and WACQT leadership, although ion traps are a competing platform and not his own; no direct link to Cirac, Zoller or Blatt apparent from profile. Chalmers colleagues (Delsing, Wilson) are not candidates in this slate.
